paper.title: Thresholding Bandit Problem with Both Duels and Pulls

settings.name_in_paper: TBP with Dueling Choices (TBP-DC), fixed confidence
unmapped: Each round the learner chooses either a direct pull of one arm (sub-Gaussian reward with parameter R) or a duel between two arms (Bernoulli outcome from arbitrary preference matrix M); pull and duel counts are measured separately
Assumption: Borda score of every positive arm (mu_i >= tau) exceeds Borda score of every negative arm
Threshold tau is known to the learner
Learner knows the sub-Gaussian parameter R (used in Figure-Out-Label confidence width)
settings.definition_quote: Given a target threshold $\thres$, our goal is to identify the positive set $\posset=\{i:\sammean{i}\geq \thres\}$ ... In each round of our algorithm, we can choose one of two possible interactions: Direct Queries (Pulls) ... sub-Gaussian with parameter $\sgpara$ ... Comparisons (Duels) ... we allow an arbitrary preference matrix $\prefmat$; the only assumption is that the score of any positive arm is larger than any negative arm

unmapped: Learner may pull an arm (Gaussian N(mu_i,R^2) reward) or duel two arms (Bernoulli outcome from preference matrix M)
Borda score of positive arms exceeds that of negative arms
settings.definition_quote: For simplicity, in this section we suppose all rewards follow a Gaussian distribution with parameter $R$, i.e., $\samdistr{\samiter}=\mathcal{N}(\sammean{\samiter},R^2)$.

symbols.H_c2: duel complexity sum over arms except i_u,i_l of 1/(bar Delta^c_i)^2
symbols.gamma_star: min over arms except i_u,i_l of bar Delta^c_i

conditions: Borda score of every positive arm exceeds every negative arm

source.label: thm:lower
source.quote: Suppose an algorithm $\algo$ recovers $\posset$ with probability $1-\tol$ for any problem instance $(\prefmat,\meanvec)$ and $\tol\leq 0.15$. ... Let $c=\min\{\frac{1}{10}, \frac{\sgpara^2}{2}\}$. Then for any problem instance ... with $\prefmat_{\samiter\samiterp}\geq \frac{3}{8}$ ... we have \E[(\compgap{k})^2 D_k+(\labelgap{k})^2 L_k]\geq c\log(\frac{1}{2\tol}).

results.notes: Delta^c_k is the Borda-score gap to the worst positive arm. c expressed with sigma = R.
